transcript:
This message comes from University at Buffalo, where scientists are working to protect the Great Lakes and freshwater supplies around the world from harmful contamination.
Learn more about their research at buffalo.edu/npr.
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Giles Snyder. Ukraine says it urgently needs more U.S. Patriot interceptor missiles to defend against incoming Russian attacks.
But as NPR's Greg Myry reports, the paperwork to transfer them is stuck at the Pentagon.
A U.S. official confirmed to NPR that the authorization to send the Patriot missiles to Ukraine is sitting on the desk of Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth at the Pentagon.
The official, who's not authorized to comment publicly on the issue, spoke to NPR's Tom Bowman.
The story was first reported by The Washington Post.
The U.S. has stopped sending Patriots directly to Ukraine, but some NATO countries have been willing to transfer small batches of 10 or so a month.
However, because these are U.S.-made weapons, the Pentagon must sign off before they can be sent to Ukraine.
Russia can fire 20 or more missiles into Ukraine on a single night.
Greg Myry, NPR News, Washington.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky says Ukraine is again receiving early warnings about Russian attacks.
Zelensky spoke to reporters after meeting with U.S. Envoy Steve Whitcoff in Norway.
Whitcoff is expected to meet with Russian President Vladimir Putin on Wednesday.
At the White House, President Trump unveiled a new program Tuesday offering payments to encourage members of the public to blow the whistle on suspected government fraud.
All of those people that are willing to do the right thing and turn people in that they know where there's been something that happened that they know all about, they're going to become rich.
The program is called the Fraud Whistleblower Incentive Program. It offers payments of up to $30,000 for anyone who submits a tip that leads to a fraud conviction or a significant federal enforcement action.
Early voting underway in Texas. Democrats hope they can pick up a Texas Senate seat, though it's been more than 30 years since a Democrat won a statewide race in Texas.
Houston Public Media's Andrew Schneider spoke with Republicans about their decision to support Republican State Attorney General Paxton over Democratic State Representative James Talarico.
Mark Petrichuk from Wood Forest, Texas says he's supporting Paxton because he's not Talarico.
I'm a free market guy, and whoever is teaching these kids that socialism and communism is okay are wrong, and so I'm actually voting against anybody that says they're a socialist or a communist.
Erika Johnson from the Woodlands says she's backing Paxton because of his record fighting human trafficking as attorney general.
I do have a friend who was a victim of that, and with his initiative whenever he first became attorney general, that was really big on my heart.
Most polling shows the race between Paxton and Talarico is a statistical dead heat. For NPR News, I'm Andrew Schneider in Houston.
And you're listening to NPR News.
Florida has carried out its 18th execution of the year under Republican Governor Ron DeSantis.
77-year-old William Reeves was pronounced dead Tuesday evening after a lethal injection at Florida State Prison near Stark.
If another execution is carried out as scheduled next month, Florida will tie the state record it set last year.
Officials in Australia say lawmaker Helen Haynes remains in critical condition after being struck by a Toyota Land Cruiser outside her office,
and the man accused of deliberately ramming his car into her appeared in court Wednesday. Adam Hancock has more from Sydney.
43-year-old Brendan Nugent has briefly appeared in court after being charged with three offenses, including causing harm to a public official.
The suspect is a resident of a rural town within Helen Haynes' electorate. He did not apply for bail and is due to return to court in February.
Police are still trying to understand any motive for the attack, with counter-terrorism officers involved in the investigation.
Victoria State Police said they could not find any direct past contact between Ms Haynes and the accused man.
The independent MP remains in critical condition in the hospital after doctors amputated one of her legs.
For NPR News, I'm Adam Hancock in Sydney.
The NFL says security will be heightened for Sunday's game in Paris between the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints.
The NFL says the league security team is on the ground, and that officials are working closely with Paris police following the protests that engulfed the French capital over the weekend.
I'm Giles Snyder, and this is NPR News.
